# OTRI, the Open Trail Running Index

> An open, free scoring tool for trail running: a race's course file (GPX) and its results file in, an explained, reproducible OTRI score for every finisher out. Anyone can score a race without an account; organizers can publish a race page; runners can try a target time on a course in the calculator. The methodology and the code are public (MIT), the model is versioned, and every score explains itself down to the maths.

OTRI is independent and not affiliated with any commercial ranking organization. It is a calculator, not an approval body: it does not rank races, approve organizers or keep a catalogue of the world's races.

## Pages

- [Home](https://otri.run/): what OTRI does, with a real example race scored by the live API.
- [Score calculator](https://otri.run/#calculator): pick a course or upload a GPX, type a target finish time, see the score and how it was worked out.
- [Score my race](https://otri.run/#score): a course file plus a results file, every finisher scored, nothing stored.
- [Scored races](https://otri.run/#races): race pages organizers published, each also at https://otri.run/races/<id>/.
- [Runners](https://otri.run/#runners): runner profiles with the runner index, each also at https://otri.run/runners/<id>/.
- [FAQ](https://otri.run/faq/): what a score means, which races can be scored, courses and GPX files, the runner index, publishing.
- [How a score is made](https://otri.run/how-otri-scores/): the model in plain language, every constant and its source, what the model does not see.
- [What is a GPX file?](https://otri.run/what-is-a-gpx/) and [Result files](https://otri.run/result-files/): what to bring.
- [API and embed](https://otri.run/#api): three public calls, no key needed, and an embeddable calculator.

## The model, in one paragraph

A score is computed from the course and the finish time alone, never from who else raced. The course is measured every 50 m and each piece is costed by its gradient (Minetti's energy-cost model), giving a flat-equivalent distance; sustained steep ground and altitude add a terrain factor. The runner's speed over that flat-equivalent distance is compared with the fastest a human has sustained over the same amount of ground, a curve through the 5000 m, marathon and 24-hour records, so 1000 is record-run level for that course size and is a reference line, not a maximum. Score = 1000 × (share of the ceiling rate)^0.85. Same course, same time, same model version: same score.

## API

- Base: https://api.otri.run
- `POST /score`: results file (CSV, TSV or XLSX) plus course file (GPX), JSON or CSV back, nothing stored.
- `POST /gpx/analyze`: one course measured, and with `finish_time_seconds` one time scored with its full breakdown.
- `GET /scoring/models`: the scoring versions.
- Reference: https://api.otri.run/docs
